messages:
aj: Heads up — starting ~03:10 UTC we saw the us-west-2 dedicated embedding pool p99 climb ~400-500ms. GPU util remains ~68%, CPU ~30%. Not a straightforward overload.

maya: I saw similar on a few requests. egress bandwidth for some tenants spiked, but not everyone. could be cross-tenant resource coupling.

infra-bot: alert: pool-usw2-dedicated tail_latency_increase detected, delta_p99=420ms, triggered at 2024-04-12T03:11:07Z

kevin: dropping a quick stacktrace + perf counters from one affected host. not pretty but maybe useful:
```
host: gpunode-uw2-17
nvlink: 92% busy
pcie_rx: 68%
kvcache_misses: 0.03
sched_steal: 0.02
latencies: p50=12ms p95=80ms p99=520ms
```

meera: nvlink 92% w/ p99 520ms smells like inter-tenant traffic pattern where embeddings + retriever batches amplify PCIe/NVLink bursts. could be "spectral" leakage between tenants on the same slice.

aj: Agree. This looks different from typical noisy-neighbor GPU hog (we'd see util near 100%). More like transient bus contention or kernel preemption jitter.

sanchit: Quick repro idea: run synthetic embedding workload at similar batch/seq and add background small-rate decoding jobs to emulate other tenants. If p99 reproduces, we can narrow to nvlink vs kernel scheduling.

kevin: On call window now — I'll schedule repro on a spare host in the same pool and pin the test tenant to a dedicated slice to compare. If isolating tenant to slice removes tail, we prove routing/scheduling problem.

maya: Also can we try soft-throttling egress on a candidate tenant to see if net bursts correlate? if yes, short-term mitigation = per-tenant egress shaping.

aj: Sounds good. Also adding a short-term routing rule: new embedding-heavy allocations get a transient isolation tag for 30m to avoid colocating with unknown high-egress tenants. Owner: kevin.

infra-bot: incident created: INC-20240412-1543, severity=low, assigned=kevin, sanchit

kevin: Repro started. Early observation: when background decoder runs, p99 jumps. When I pin the test tenant to a separate slice (isolation tag), p99 drops <100ms.

meera: That suggests a scheduler-level isolation gap rather than model kernel bug. Could be batching/kvcache interference or DMA bursts on NVSwitch.

aj: Short-term asks: 1) keep routing isolation tag for embedding launches (30m default) 2) add egress shaping experiment (maya) 3) instrument nvlink/dma counters per-tenant (sanchit) 4) run repro across 3 hosts (kevin).

maya: noted. I'll open a short PR to add the isolation tag logic and a flag for opt-out for experiments. Cost note: may increase scheduling tail by ~12% capacity due to less bin-packing. worth it for customer SLOs.

sanchit: I'll add per-tenant NVLink counters to our telemetry. might be a bit of work on the agent side but should be straightforward.

aj: Good. Long-term idea: consider lane-reservation scheduler for high-QPS embedding tenants (tradeoff ~+15% infra cost). Put on roadmap if repro confirms.

oncall-bot: update: INC-20240412-1543 moved to monitoring state; mitigation: transient isolation tag applied to new allocations in pool-usw2-dedicated.

kevin: Will post repro data and a short write-up in #eng-infra when done. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
